about: Olin Corporation is a Clayton, Missouri manufacturer of chlor alkali products and epoxy, and of Winchester ammunition. Its Chlor Alkali division makes chlorine and caustic soda, Epoxy makes resins, and Winchester produces ammunition for hunters, sport shooters, law enforcement and the military. It is listed on the NYSE (OLN), with revenue of around $6.5 billion. Founded in 1892. Winchester has high consumer visibility among shooters, while the rest of the company is a B2B chemicals supplier.

Perimeter Solutions is a Clayton, Missouri specialty chemicals company, listed on the NYSE (PRM), best known for long-term fire retardants for wildfires (Fire-Trol, Phos-Chek) used by US and international forestry agencies, and for firefighting foams and other chemicals. It earns revenue from government and industrial customers, and was formed from the 2021 acquisition of Solvay's phosphorous pentasulfide business and fire retardant businesses. B2B and government supplier with low consumer awareness.

Hanwha Solutions is a South Korean company, part of Hanwha Group, headquartered in Seoul and listed on the Korea Exchange. It operates in renewable energy (Qcells solar modules), chemicals and advanced materials. Qcells has major solar manufacturing in Georgia, USA, and Korea. Revenue is about KRW 13 trillion. Hanwha group is a large sports sponsor in Korea. Industrial brand with growing international visibility.

Ahlstrom is a Helsinki-based global manufacturer of fibre-based materials, formed from the 2017 merger of Ahlstrom and Munksjö and now owned by Finnish and Swedish investors. It makes filtration media, medical fibres, food packaging, industrial and decor papers for customers across many industries. Around 6,000 employees and revenue of about 3 billion euros. B2B brand with low consumer visibility.

Easpring Finland New Materials is a Finnish subsidiary of China's Easpring Material Technology, set up in Kotka for battery cathode materials production for European electric vehicle supply chains. Funding is shown as roughly 514 million. It is a manufacturing project aimed at lithium-ion battery customers. B2B with no consumer brand profile.

about: Cabot Corporation is a Boston-based specialty chemicals and performance materials company, listed on the NYSE (CBT). It is a leading producer of carbon black used in tyres and rubber, plus fumed silica, activated carbon and battery materials such as conductive carbons. Customers are tyre makers, industrial and battery manufacturers. Operates plants across the Americas, Europe and Asia, with revenue of about $4 billion. Founded in 1882. B2B with low consumer visibility.

Chemed Corporation is a Cincinnati-based US healthcare and services holding company, listed on the NYSE (CHE), whose main businesses are VITAS Healthcare, the largest US provider of hospice care, and Roto-Rooter, the plumbing and drain cleaning brand. Revenue is about $2.4 billion. Roto-Rooter is a well-known consumer brand in the US home-services market, with strong brand marketing.

Indorama Corporation is a Singapore-based fertiliser and chemicals producer linked to the Lohia family's Indorama group, making urea and other fertilisers and industrial chemicals at plants in Nigeria, Indonesia and elsewhere. Customers are agricultural and industrial buyers. Revenue is significant at group level. B2B industrial company with limited public brand awareness, though the Indorama name is known in commodity circles.

about: Lilac Solutions is an Oakland, California-based direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology company, whose ion exchange process extracts lithium from brines more efficiently than evaporation ponds. Backed by Bill Gates's Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Mitsubishi and others, with about $418 million raised. Customers are lithium producers. B2B climate technology, with little consumer awareness.

IMCD is a Rotterdam, Netherlands specialty chemicals and ingredients distributor, which sources products from suppliers and sells to makers of coatings, pharma, food, personal care and industrial goods in more than 60 countries. Revenue is about 4.5 billion euros. It is listed on Euronext Amsterdam (IMCD). B2B distributor with no consumer brand.

PT Chandra Asri Alkali (CAA) is an Indonesian chemical company, a subsidiary of PT Chandra Asri Pacific, producing chlor-alkali products such as caustic soda and ethylene dichloride for industrial customers. It sits within Indonesia's largest integrated petrochemical group, which has Thailand's SCG as a major shareholder. B2B with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Schrodinger is a New York software company (Nasdaq: SDGR) whose physics-based computational platform is used to discover and design drugs and materials, with customers among pharma and biotech companies, and with its own drug pipeline. Founded in 1990 and with revenue around 200 million dollars. B2B science software, known in pharma and materials circles, with no consumer brand.

Ag Growth International is a Winnipeg, Manitoba maker of grain handling, storage, conditioning and food processing equipment, including Westeel bins, Wheatheart augers and Hutchinson conveyors. Customers are farmers, grain handlers, ethanol and food processors across North America, Brazil, Europe and other markets. Revenue is roughly 1.4 billion Canadian dollars a year. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (AFN). It is an industrial B2B business selling mainly through dealers, with little consumer brand awareness outside agriculture.

Elkem is a Norwegian advanced materials company based in Oslo, founded in 1904, producing silicones, silicon metal, ferrosilicon, carbon solutions and microsilica from plants in Norway, China, France and North America, using hydropower. Customers are chemical, construction, electronics, automotive and energy companies in the world. Revenue is about 35 billion Norwegian kroner. It is majority owned by China National Bluestar (CNCG), and is listed on Euronext Oslo Bors (ELK). B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

ASK Chemicals is a German foundry chemicals company based in Hilden, North Rhine-Westphalia, supplying binders, coatings, feeders and filters for metal casting, with plants worldwide. Customers are automotive, machinery and engine foundries. It is privately held, owned by private equity. Recorded funding is about 315 million. B2B industrial chemicals brand with no consumer awareness, so any sponsorship rationale would be corporate hospitality or recruitment.

IQE is a Cardiff, Wales-based global maker of compound semiconductor wafers using epitaxy, supplying materials used in 5G handsets, wireless chips, photonics, infrared and VCSELs for 3D sensing, with customers including chip makers such as Skyworks, Qorvo and Broadcom. Revenue is about 150 million pounds with sites in the UK, US, Taiwan and Singapore. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM (IQE). B2B technology brand, with no consumer awareness.

Fullcryo is a company based in Beijing, China, described in Crunchbase as a cryogenic equipment manufacturer in advanced materials and manufacturing. Recorded funding is about 2.1 billion Chinese yuan. Its products, customers and ownership are not confirmed here, though the sector suggests tanks, vessels and systems for storing and moving liquefied gases for industrial or energy users. B2B industrial brand with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: TETRA Technologies is a Spring, Texas energy services and chemicals company that provides calcium chloride, completion fluids and water management for oil and gas operators, plus lithium and bromine development in Arkansas, and Deepwater production support. Customers are oil and gas operators and industrial users, with revenue of about 600 million dollars. It is listed on the NYSE (TTI). B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness.

Fertiglobe is the world's largest seaborne exporter of nitrogen fertilizers, based in Abu Dhabi. It produces urea, ammonia and other products at plants in the UAE, Egypt and Algeria, and sells to farmers and distributors in Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas. ADNOC owns a majority stake of 86 percent, with OCI previously the majority holder before selling in 2023. Listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (FERTIGLB). B2B commodity producer with minimal consumer visibility.

EQUATE Petrochemical Company is a Kuwaiti petrochemical producer, based in Safat, Kuwait, making ethylene glycol and polyethylene from facilities at Shuaiba and operating the TKOC unit. It is a joint venture of Petrochemical Industries Company (PIC), Dow, Boubyan Petrochemical and Gulf Investment Corporation, selling to plastics and packaging manufacturers in Asia, Europe and the Middle East. It is a large industrial exporter with annual capacity in the millions of tonnes. B2B chemical supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Advanced Petrochemical Company is a Saudi chemicals producer based in Jubail, listed on Tadawul (2330). It runs a propane dehydrogenation unit making propylene and polypropylene, and supplies petrochemical products and related industrial gases and utilities to plastics converters and industrial customers in Saudi Arabia and export markets. Founded in 2003 and controlled by Saudi industrial investors. Crunchbase shows SAR 2.2 billion in funding as read. B2B petrochemical supplier with no consumer brand profile.

NatureWorks is a US bioplastics company, based in Plymouth, Minnesota, and a joint venture of Cargill and Thailand's PTT Global Chemical. It makes Ingeo polylactic acid (PLA) biopolymer from plant sugars at a plant in Blair, Nebraska and is building a new plant in Thailand. Customers are packaging, textile, food service and consumer goods firms. Private JV. B2B material supplier, with brand recognition in sustainability circles but not among consumers.

Lyten is a US battery company, based in San Jose, California, developing lithium-sulfur batteries and 3D graphene materials for electric vehicles, drones, aerospace and defence. In 2025 it agreed to acquire assets of Northvolt in Sweden, Poland and Germany after the Swedish company went bankrupt. It has no mass production yet and has raised more than $360 million in funding. Customers are automakers, aerospace and defence buyers. B2B technology developer with little consumer awareness.

Western Forest Products is a Canadian lumber producer based in Vancouver, with sawmills and timberlands on the coast of British Columbia, selling Douglas fir, hemlock and western red cedar to builders and manufacturers in North America, Japan and China. Revenue is about CAD 1.2 billion. Listed on the TSX (WEF). B2B wood products supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Worley is an Australian engineering and professional services group, based in Sydney, delivering design, project management and sustainability services for energy, chemicals and resources customers in around 40 countries. It employs about 50,000 people and has revenue near AUD 12 billion, after acquiring Jacobs' Energy, Chemicals and Resources business in 2019. Listed on the ASX (WOR). B2B engineering brand, with no consumer profile.

Amogy is a US clean energy technology company, based in Brooklyn, New York, founded in 2020, which has developed ammonia-to-power systems that crack ammonia into hydrogen to generate electricity for ships, trucks and stationary power. Investors include SK Innovation, Temasek and Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund. It has raised about $313 million. Customers are maritime and heavy industry. Pre-commercial B2B brand, little consumer awareness.

AMSC (American Superconductor) is a US energy technology company, based in Ayer, Massachusetts, founded in 1987, supplying power electronics, grid resilience systems, ship protection systems for the US Navy, and wind turbine control systems and electrical equipment. Customers are utilities, wind turbine makers, the US Navy and semiconductor fabs, with revenue of around $200 million. It is listed on Nasdaq (AMSC). B2B industrial brand with little consumer visibility.

Orica is an Australian company, based in Melbourne, that is the world's largest provider of commercial explosives and blasting systems for mining, quarrying and infrastructure, plus ground support and chemicals such as ammonium nitrate and sodium cyanide. It operates in over 100 countries, with revenue about AUD 7 billion. Listed on the ASX (ORI). B2B mining services brand, with little consumer awareness.

DP Technology is a Chinese 'AI for Science' company, based in Beijing and founded in 2018, building scientific computing and machine learning tools for chemistry, materials and drug discovery, such as the Bohrium platform and the Uni-Mol molecular model. Customers are research institutions, pharma and materials companies. Crunchbase shows about $254 million in funding, latest in December 2025. B2B scientific software with no consumer awareness.

Customers would ultimately be oncology patients and health systems, though as a drug developer it has no revenue yet. B2B biotech with no consumer brand visibility.

Customers are consumer product brands, and its profile is concentrated in sustainability and climate circles rather than mainstream consumers.

It is listed in Frankfurt (HEN3), controlled by the Henkel family. Many household brands are widely recognised, and Henkel is an experienced sports and events sponsor.

Westwater Resources is a Centennial, Colorado company developing battery-grade natural graphite and other energy-related minerals, with its flagship Kellyton graphite processing plant in Alabama and the Coosa graphite deposit. It is listed on NYSE American (WWR). Customers would be battery makers and the electric vehicle supply chain. Funding of about $206M was recorded in 2026 according to the data. Pre-revenue B2B developer, known to resource investors but with little consumer brand awareness.

about: Virtual Incision is a Lincoln, Nebraska medical device company that has developed MIRA, a miniaturised robotic-assisted surgical system for abdominal procedures such as colon resections, designed to be small and portable enough to move between operating rooms. It spun out of the University of Nebraska and has raised about $163M, with a 2026 funding recorded. Customers are hospitals and surgeons. Specialised B2B medical technology brand with no consumer recognition.

Societe nationale industrielle et miniere (SNIM) is Mauritania's state-owned mining company, with operations in iron ore around Zouerate and rail and port facilities in Nouadhibou, the country's key export route. It is the nation's largest industrial employer and a main source of foreign exchange, shipping iron ore concentrate mainly to Europe and Asia. Funding of about $425M was recorded in 2025, likely for expansion. B2B state enterprise with strong national profile in Mauritania but little consumer-facing activity.

Vital Thin Film Materials (Guangdong) is a Shenzhen-area Chinese maker of high-purity sputtering targets and evaporation materials used in thin-film coating for displays, semiconductors, solar cells and optical applications. Customers are display, chip and component manufacturers, and revenue comes from material sales. It is a privately held company that has raised capital from investors, with Crunchbase showing about CN¥5.7 billion in funding and a round in September 2022. B2B industrial materials supplier with little consumer awareness, so a limited fit for brand sponsorship.

about: Superior Plus is a Toronto-based Canadian company, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (SPB), that distributes propane and other energy products. Its main businesses are Superior Propane in Canada, propane distribution in the US and wholesale operations. Customers are households, farms and industrial clients that buy propane for heating, cooking and fuel. Revenue runs to roughly C$3 billion annually, with hundreds of thousands of customers. It is a dividend-paying income company, formed in 1996 as a trust. Regionally familiar energy brand, with little national consumer sponsorship profile.

EcoCeres is a Hong Kong-headquartered producer of sustainable and renewable fuels, converting used cooking oil and other biomass waste into biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel, with plants in China and Malaysia. Customers are airlines, fuel traders and industrial clients, mainly in Europe, and it earns revenue from fuel sales. In 2023 it raised about $500 million from institutional investors, giving it roughly $508 million in Crunchbase funding. Private company; B2B and little consumer awareness, though sustainable aviation fuel is of growing interest to airlines and motorsport.

Battelle Memorial Institute is a non-profit applied science and technology organisation based in Columbus, Ohio, running contract research for the US government and industry in areas such as national security, health, energy, advanced materials and cybersecurity. It manages or co-manages several US national laboratories, including Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, and has thousands of employees. Founded in 1929 from the will of industrialist Gordon Battelle; it developed xerography with Haloid. B2B and government research institute with little consumer brand awareness.

Halio is a Hayward, California maker of electronically tintable smart glass for commercial buildings, formerly known as Kinestral Technologies. Its glass changes tint on demand to control heat and glare and is sold to building owners, architects and developers. Founded in 2012, it has raised about $400 million from investors including Corning. Crunchbase shows about $399 million. B2B construction-technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Shanghai Putailai New Energy Technology is a Chinese maker of lithium-ion battery materials, especially graphite anode materials, as well as separators, binders and coated films for battery cells. Customers are major battery producers such as CATL, LG and BYD, and it earns revenue from material sales. Headquartered in Shanghai, it is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and is one of the leading anode makers in the world, with Crunchbase showing about CN¥2.8 billion raised in 2023. B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness.

Synthomer is a London-headquartered specialty chemicals company making polymers and ingredients, such as latex for nitrile gloves, adhesives, coatings, construction chemicals, and performance materials, with plants in Europe, Asia and North America. Customers are manufacturers of gloves, paints, adhesives and building products. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (SYNT), with revenue around GBP 2 billion, and with roots in the Yule Catto group. B2B industrial brand with minimal consumer awareness.

VACUUMSCHMELZE (VAC) is a German advanced materials company, based in Hanau, that makes magnetic materials and components, including soft-magnetic alloys, rare-earth permanent magnets, and parts for electric motors, sensors, transformers and electric vehicles. Customers are car makers, electronics and industrial firms. Founded in 1914, it has about 5,000 employees and a global footprint, with a US magnet plant in South Carolina. Crunchbase records a $335 million financing in September 2024. B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

PTT Global Chemical (GC) is Thailand's largest integrated petrochemical company, based in Bangkok and majority-owned by state energy group PTT. It makes olefins, polyethylene, polypropylene, styrene, ethylene oxide derivatives and aromatics, and has bioplastics and recycling initiatives, with plants in Thailand, plus operations in the US, China and Europe. Customers are packaging, automotive and industrial manufacturers. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (PTTGC), with revenue of several hundred billion baht. B2B industrial brand, though PTT is a known sponsor in Thailand.

Barito Pacific is an Indonesian conglomerate based in Jakarta, controlled by tycoon Prajogo Pangestu, with interests in petrochemicals through Chandra Asri, the country's largest integrated petrochemical producer, in geothermal and renewable energy through Barito Renewables and Star Energy, and formerly in timber and plantations. Customers are packaging, automotive and industrial manufacturers, and utilities. Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BRPT). B2B industrial and energy group with limited consumer awareness, though its owner is prominent in Indonesian business.

INERATEC is a Karlsruhe, Germany, climate technology company producing carbon-neutral synthetic fuels, such as e-fuels and e-kerosene, using modular chemical reactors that convert CO2 and green hydrogen into synthetic hydrocarbons. Customers are airlines, shipping firms and chemical and fuel companies. Founded in 2016 as a spin-off from Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, it raised about EUR 208 million, including a 2024 round, and opened Europe's largest e-fuel plant in Frankfurt. B2B energy brand, interesting in motorsport fuels.

Zhejiang Yonghe Refrigerant is a Quzhou, Zhejiang Chinese fluorochemical maker, producing refrigerants, fluoropolymers and fluorine-based chemicals used in air conditioning, refrigeration and industrial applications. Customers are appliance manufacturers, chemical firms and industrial buyers in China and abroad. It is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Crunchbase shows about CN¥1.7 billion in funding in 2025. B2B chemicals brand with little consumer awareness.

Origin Materials is a West Sacramento, California materials technology company that converts sustainable wood residues and other biomass into carbon-negative materials such as PET plastic feedstock (using its CMF and HCl chemistry) and caps and closures. Customers are packaging and chemical firms. It listed on Nasdaq (ORGN) through a SPAC merger in 2021. Crunchbase shows about $215 million of funding. B2B sustainability brand with limited consumer awareness, though its materials appear in beverage packaging.

NanoXplore is a Montreal-based graphene company that makes graphene powder and graphene-enhanced plastics and composites, producing parts for the automotive, heavy truck and industrial markets through its plants in Canada and the US. Customers are vehicle makers and industrial manufacturers. Listed on the TSX (GRA). Crunchbase shows about $188 million of funding. B2B advanced materials brand with limited consumer awareness.

Kronos Worldwide is a Dallas-based producer of titanium dioxide (TiO2) pigments, used in paints, coatings, plastics, paper and inks, with plants in Europe and North America. Customers are chemical and coatings manufacturers. Listed on the NYSE (KRO), it is majority owned by Valhi (part of the Contran group). Revenue is about $1.7 billion. B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness; the Crunchbase funding of 150 million probably reflects a debt financing.

Tata Chemicals is a Mumbai-based Indian chemicals company in the Tata Group, making soda ash, sodium bicarbonate, salt (Tata Salt), and nutrition and speciality products, with operations in India, the UK, the US and Africa. Customers are glass, detergent and food manufacturers, as well as consumers buying Tata Salt. Listed on the NSE and BSE (TATACHEM), with revenue of around INR 150 billion. Founded in 1939. Tata Salt is a household name in India.

Normet is a Finnish company, based in Espoo, that makes equipment and chemicals for underground construction and mining, including shotcrete sprayers, concrete transport vehicles, charging equipment, and construction chemicals such as accelerators and waterproofing. Customers are mining companies and tunnel builders across the world, and it has subsidiaries in dozens of countries. It is privately held. Crunchbase shows about 220 million euros of financing in early 2026. A B2B industrial brand with strong standing within mining and tunnelling, and no consumer profile.

Cydsa is a Mexican chemicals and industrial group, based in Monterrey, that makes chlorine-soda, refrigerant gases, specialty chemicals, and plastic and synthetic fibre products such as viscose and polyester fibres, and sells them to industrial and consumer products companies in Mexico and abroad. It is listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange as CYDSASA. Revenue is around 1 billion dollars a year. Funding shown is about 144 million dollars, from September 2026. A B2B industrial group with no direct consumer brand.

Australian advanced manufacturing company that uses its cold spray technology (a metal 3D printing method) to build and repair large metal parts for aerospace, defence, mining, rail and marine customers. It also supplies Titomic Kinetic Fusion systems, with a growing business in the US defence supply chain. Based in Mount Waverley, Melbourne, and listed on the ASX (TTT), with a funding round in 2026 near 96 million dollars. Early-stage industrial technology company; B2B and little consumer awareness.

US-listed (Nasdaq: FEAM) development-stage company building a boron and lithium project at Fort Cady, California, with a planned processing plant in Hesperia. Boron is used in glass, ceramics, magnets, semiconductors and fertilisers, and the company pitches itself as a domestic supplier for the US supply chain. Based in Apple Valley, California, with large capital raising needs and little revenue to date. Mining and materials developer with no consumer brand; known mainly to resource investors.

Canadian clean technology company in London, Ontario, developing the Hydrochemolytic technology, which uses water, heat and pressure to upgrade heavy oil and recycle waste plastics back into usable feedstocks. It aims to licence the process to refiners and plastics recyclers, so revenue is early stage and based on pilot projects. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX Venture (ADUR). Funding near 66 million dollars. Early-stage cleantech with no consumer brand profile.

Chemical and energy company with a US address in Fort Lee, New Jersey, recorded with a 2026 funding event of about 64 million dollars. Charbone is known as a developer of hydrogen production and distribution, with operations in Quebec and Canadian-listed shares. It sells industrial gases and clean hydrogen to industrial customers. Small-cap with a clean energy focus, funded by share placings. B2B and limited consumer brand awareness.

Canadian mineral exploration company based in Rouyn-Noranda, Quebec, focused on advanced materials and geological exploration, likely gold and base metals in Quebec's Abitibi region. Listed on the TSX Venture, it raised about 57 million dollars in 2026. Pre-revenue explorer funded by share issues. No consumer brand visibility. Foseco India makes foundry chemicals such as refractories, fluxes and filters used in metal casting. It is the Indian arm of Foseco, a global brand now owned by Vesuvius plc. It sells to iron, steel and aluminium foundries, auto parts makers and heavy industry. Shirpur is its plant location in Maharashtra, and it is listed on the BSE and NSE (FOSECOIND). Revenue is about 5 billion rupees. B2B industrial supplier with low consumer awareness.

Indian specialty chemicals company in Thane, Maharashtra, making advanced intermediates, electrolyte salts and lithium battery chemicals, organics for pharma and agrochemicals, plus bromine and lithium-based products. Customers are pharmaceutical, agrochemical and battery producers in India and export markets. Listed on the NSE and BSE (NEOGEN) since 2019. Founded in 1989. Revenue is roughly 8 to 10 billion rupees. B2B chemicals supplier with almost no consumer awareness.

Clean Power Hydrogen is a Doncaster, UK-based company developing a membrane-free electrolyser for green hydrogen production, built by an engineering team in northern England. Target customers are industrial energy, fuel and transport users. The company floated on the London AIM in 2021. Funding figure of around 33.5 million. Small-cap clean energy technology developer, pre-revenue to low revenue, with no consumer brand visibility.

Montreal-based high-temperature plasma technology company that provides plasma atomisation of metal powders for 3D printing, drop-in decarbonisation systems for industrial processes, and waste-to-resource systems. The group was formed by combining several established ceramic brands under one holding and has received private-equity backed funding of about 150 million. about: Avalon Advanced Materials is a Toronto-based Canadian exploration and development company focused on minerals for the clean-energy transition, notably the Separation Rapids lithium project in Ontario. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (AVL). It is pre-revenue and funds itself through equity raises and partnerships. It is a small resource company with essentially no consumer brand awareness and little capacity for large sponsorship deals.

Gurit is a Swiss composite materials company based in Zurich that develops and supplies structural core materials, kits, engineered composites and adhesives for wind turbine blades, marine, aerospace, automotive and industrial uses. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (GUR), it has annual sales in the hundreds of millions of Swiss francs and sites in Europe, Asia and North America. It has long worked in sailing and yacht racing, supplying composite materials to race boats. It is a B2B supplier with moderate visibility in marine and motorsport circles.

Navin Fluorine International is a Mumbai specialty chemicals company in the Mafatlal group that makes refrigerant gases, specialty fluorochemicals, pharmaceutical intermediates and offers contract development and manufacturing services. Customers include global pharma, agrochemical and refrigeration companies. It is listed on NSE and BSE, with annual revenue of several billion rupees and manufacturing in Gujarat. It is a B2B chemical supplier with no consumer profile and little sponsorship relevance.

Australian Strategic Materials is a Perth-based company that is building a vertically integrated supply chain for critical metals, including rare earths, with a mine at Dubbo in New South Wales and a metal and alloys plant in Korea. It makes neodymium-based metals and alloys for magnets used in electric vehicles and wind turbines. Listed on the ASX (ASM), it sells to magnet makers. It is a B2B resource firm with little consumer awareness.

Calix is an Australian cleantech company based in Pymble, New South Wales, that develops a flash calcination technology for making reactive minerals, used in low-emission cement and lime, battery materials, water treatment and agriculture, and a carbon-capture process. It sells to industrial customers and research partners, and is listed on the ASX (CXL). It also has a US-focused battery materials program. It is a B2B science-led company with low consumer brand awareness.

Matinas BioPharma is a New Jersey clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing lipid nanocrystal (LNC) drug delivery technology and candidates such as MAT2203, an oral amphotericin B for fungal infections, and MAT2501. It is listed on the NYSE American (MTNB) and is funded by equity raises and partnerships. It is a small drug developer without commercial products, and consumers do not know the brand.

American Lithium is a Vancouver-based exploration and development company advancing lithium projects, notably TLC in Nevada, Falchani in Peru and the Macusani plateau, which also holds uranium rights. It is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (LI) and Nasdaq (AMLI), and funds itself through equity raises. It has no revenue and no consumer products. It is a small resource developer with little public brand awareness and limited sponsorship capacity.

Zahrat Al Waha for Trading and Contracting is a Riyadh-based Saudi manufacturer of plastics and building-related products, listed on the Saudi Exchange (Nomu). It produces plastic and plastic-related products for commercial and construction customers in the Kingdom. The input shows funding of SAR 150 million, last dated November 2025. It is a regional B2B company with little consumer brand awareness.

Acutaas Chemicals is an Indian specialty chemicals and pharmaceutical intermediates company based in Sachin, Gujarat, formerly Ami Organics, making advanced intermediates and active ingredients for pharma and electronic chemical customers worldwide. Listed on NSE and BSE since 2021, it supplies innovator and generic drug makers. Revenue is in the order of several billion rupees. It is a B2B manufacturer with no consumer visibility.

Gelion is a London-headquartered battery technology company, listed on the London AIM market (GELN), developing lithium-sulfur and zinc-bromide battery technology, with roots in the University of Sydney, and owning the Oxis Energy intellectual property bought in 2023. It targets aviation, defence and stationary storage customers. It is pre-commercial, with funding of about $35 million, and little consumer awareness, so it is not an obvious sponsor.

Guangdong Guanghua Sci-Tech is a Chinese specialty chemicals and electronic materials maker based in Shantou, best known for high-purity chemicals used in the electronics industry, such as solvents, acids and other wet process chemicals for printed circuit boards, semiconductors and display panels. Its customers are electronics manufacturers rather than consumers, and it sells under the Guanghua name. B2B supplier with essentially no consumer brand awareness outside China, so limited sponsorship relevance.

Queensland Pacific Metals is an Australian-listed battery metals developer planning to process nickel and cobalt laterite ore from New Caledonia and elsewhere at a hydrometallurgical refinery in Townsville, Queensland, producing battery-grade nickel sulphate and cobalt sulphate, plus ammonium sulphate by-products. The target customers are lithium-ion battery cathode makers and electric vehicle supply chains. It is listed on the ASX (QPM) and has been working on its Townsville Energy Chemicals Hub project, with Australian government support. It is pre-revenue and project-stage, a pure B2B company with minimal public brand awareness, so brand sponsorship relevance is limited.

Rottneros is a Swedish pulp producer operating two mills, Vallvik and Rottneros, making chemical (sulphate) pulp and chemimechanical pulp (CTMP) from Nordic softwood and spruce. Customers are paper and board makers and manufacturers of tissue, specialty papers, filters and packaging, mainly in Europe, which buy it as an input. Revenue comes from pulp sales and it also sells energy and by-products. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and the Oslo Stock Exchange (ROT). It supplies B2B materials with no consumer brand and is not a typical sponsor.

Unipar Carbocloro is a Brazilian producer of chlor-alkali chemicals and related products, making chlorine, caustic soda, PVC resin, sodium hypochlorite and hydrochloric acid at plants in Cubatao and Cajati in Sao Paulo state. It sells to industrial customers in water treatment, plastics, construction, pulp and paper, textiles and other sectors, and is among the leading Brazilian producers of PVC. The company is part of the Unipar group, which is listed on B3 in Sao Paulo (UNIP3/UNIP6). B2B chemical manufacturer with no consumer brand awareness, so unlikely to be an F1 sponsor.

Borregaard is a Norwegian biorefinery that turns sustainably harvested wood into specialty chemicals: lignin-based binders and dispersants (Borresperse, Vanisperse), vanillin for flavours, cellulose fibres (Exilva microfibrillar cellulose) and bioethanol. It runs its main plant in Sarpsborg and sells to construction, agriculture, food, pharma and battery makers worldwide, with export markets across Europe, Asia and the Americas. Revenue is roughly 3 to 4 billion Norwegian kroner. Founded in 1889 and listed on Oslo Bors (BRG). B2B ingredient supplier whose brand is little known to consumers, though its sustainability story fits climate-focused partnerships.

Entegris is a US supplier of advanced materials and process solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, including filters, chemical delivery systems, high-purity chemicals and gases, specialty coatings, and wafer and chip containers. Customers are the chipmakers and equipment makers, such as TSMC, Intel and Samsung, which buy products and replacements repeatedly. Revenue is several billion dollars, after the 2022 acquisition of CMC Materials. Listed on Nasdaq (ENTG) and headquartered in Billerica, Massachusetts, with a global footprint including Asia. B2B industrial brand with no consumer presence and low general public awareness.

Fusion Fuel Green is a green hydrogen technology company, originally based in Portugal, developing electrolysers that produce hydrogen from solar power for use in industry and mobility. Its main product has been the HEVO modular electrolyser systems, sold to project developers and industrial customers, mostly in Europe and the Middle East. It listed on Nasdaq (HTOO) via a SPAC merger in 2020 and has faced financial difficulty and restructuring. Small, B2B, with minimal brand awareness. Its fit with F1 would be sustainability messaging, but the commercial scale is modest.

Surface Transforms is a British manufacturer of carbon-ceramic brake discs for high-performance cars. It supplies road car makers with discs made near Liverpool, with customers including Porsche and McLaren among performance and luxury brands. Customers are automotive OEMs, and revenue is a few million pounds. Listed on London's AIM (SCE). Small, technical, B2B supplier known inside automotive engineering and motorsport circles, with limited consumer awareness. Natural motorsport relevance and a plausible technical or associate partner, though its finances have been stretched.

UAC of Nigeria is a Nigerian diversified food and beverage group, originally the United Africa Company, with businesses in packaged foods (Gala sausage rolls and Funtime snacks, Supreme ice cream and Swan water), animal feeds, quick-service restaurants such as Mr Bigg's, plus property and paints interests. Based in Lagos and listed on the Nigerian Exchange (UACN), with a history dating back to the 1800s. Gala is one of Nigeria's best-known snack brands, so strong local consumer recognition, which suits mass-market sponsorship in West Africa.

Ashland is a US specialty chemicals company making additives and ingredients for pharmaceuticals, personal care, food, coatings and construction, with products such as cellulose ethers, vinyl pyrrolidones and Natrosol thickeners. Customers are manufacturers in these industries, selling to brands rather than consumers. It was founded in 1924 as Ashland Oil, restructured to focus on specialty chemicals after selling Valvoline and other divisions, and is listed on the NYSE (ASH). Roughly 4,000 employees, with revenue around 2 billion dollars and the headquarters now moved from Kentucky to Delaware. B2B ingredient brand with little consumer awareness.
